title: ठाडो भाका लोक नृत्य {Thado Bhaka Folk Dance}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख ठाडोभाकालोकनृत्यको अध्ययनमा केन्द्रित छ । ठाडोभाकागीतको एउटा लय वा शैलीहो । यसै गीतगायनसँगै गरिने नृत्यलाई यस अध्ययनका सन्दर्भमा ठाडोभाका लोकनृत्य भनिएको छ । गुरुङ समुदायमा भने रोधीका नामबाट यो नृत्य प्रचलित छ । यसरी यस नृत्यको प्रचलन जातिगत रूपमा दुरा, गुरुङ, मगर, कुमाललगायत समुदायमा रहेको देखिन्छभने क्षेत्रगतरूपमालमजुङ, कास्की, तनहुँ, गोरखा, म्याग्दी, सुदूर पश्चिम, कर्णाली क्षेत्र, सुदूरपूर्व, भारतको आसाम लगायत स्थानमा प्रचलित देखिन्छ । यसका विभिन्न नाम र प्रस्तुतिगत शैलीछन् । क्षेत्रकार्यबाट सङ्कलित सामग्रीका आधारमा यस लेखमा यस नृत्यको प्रचलनका बारेमा चर्चा गरी गीतसहित प्रस्तुत गरिने आख्यानमुक्त लोकनृत्यका कथ्यविषय वा मूलभाव, शैली, भाषा, उद्देश्य, स्थायी—अन्तरा र थेगो, लय वा सङगीत र रङ्गमञ्च र वेशभूषा जस्ता तŒवका आधारमा विश्लेषण गरिएको छ ।
american_english: The present article focuses on the study of the Thado Bhaka folk dance. Thado Bhaka is a rhythm or style of song. The dance performed alongside the singing of this very song is termed the Thado Bhaka folk dance in the context of this study. In the Gurung community, however, this dance is prevalent under the name of Rodhi. Thus, the practice of this dance is seen ethnically among communities including Dura, Gurung, Magar, and Kumal, while regionally it appears prevalent in Lamjung, Kaski, Tanahun, Gorkha, Myagdi, the Far West, the Karnali region, the Far East, and Assam in India, among other places. It has various names and presentation styles. On the basis of materials collected from fieldwork, this article discusses the prevalence of this dance and analyzes this non-narrative folk dance presented with song on the basis of elements such as subject matter or central motif, style, language, purpose, verse-chorus (sthayi-antara) and refrain (thego), rhythm or music, and stage and costume.

informal_english: This paper here is focused on studying the Thado Bhaka folk dance. Thado Bhaka itself is just a rhythm or style of singing songs. The dance that people do while singing this very tune is what we're calling the Thado Bhaka folk dance in this study. Over in the Gurung community, though, this dance goes by the name of Rodhi. So you find folks doing this dance ethnically among communities like the Dura, Gurung, Magar, and Kumal, while regionally you see it across Lamjung, Kaski, Tanahun, Gorkha, Myagdi, the Far West, the Karnali region, the Far East, and even over in Assam in India. It goes by all sorts of names and has different styles of performance. Working from material gathered in fieldwork, this article talks about how the dance is done and breaks down this non-narrative folk dance performed to song according to elements like its main subject or motif, style, language, aim, verse-chorus and refrain, rhythm or music, and the stage setup and costumes.
